floors.cause: Seen questions: v0.2 was designed from two of them (fs-028, fs-035), so this is not the headline. In v02-seen (3 trials) accuracy is 111 of 129 (86.0%) and wrong answers are 2 of 113 answered (1.8%). fs-028, fs-035 and fs-041 are right in every trial. Of the misses, 15 are correct refusals of questions v0.2 still cannot express, 2 are misreads and 1 is a question that can be read with either of two dates. v0.1 (select-haiku-2026-11-11, 1 trial) had 2 wrong of 37 answered (5.4%).
floors.next: The held-out result (v02-holdout) is the headline. The v0.2 prompt and grammar are not changed after seeing these results.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (v02-seen, v0.2 grammar): Refused in 1 of 3 trials, saying invoices cannot reach customers. They can, through work orders and sites. Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): The first intent named a field that does not exist; on the retry the model said invoices cannot be grouped by customer. They can: the registry links invoices to customers through work orders and sites. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): The model left out the "paid" filter and grouped by site and customer ID instead of by customer, with no "more than $20,000" condition.
misses.refusal: Customer names are not reachable from invoices in one join. The path is invoices → work_orders → sites → customers, and the registry only lists direct joins (invoices to work_orders, but not work_orders to customers). The intent cannot name a multi-hop field like customers.name, so the per-customer totals cannot be grouped.
